sector.name: PEB
sector.description: PEB and prefab players serving industrial and infrastructure capex

fyPerformance: Q1FY27 revenue grew 20.7% YoY to ₹460 Cr from ₹381 Cr
EBITDA increased 24.6% to ₹39 Cr, ahead of revenue growth, while margin remained stable at 8.6%
PAT was flat at ₹28 Cr due to lower treasury income as IPO funds were deployed into capex
Order book increased to ₹1,864 Cr by July 2026, including a ₹165 Cr energy-sector order
Q1 production was around 40,000 tonnes, implying about 80% utilization of quarterly capacity

guidanceTracking.actual: Gujarat started in July; AP heavy structures entered trial production
₹460 Cr in Q1; management says well on target

guidance.value: Average around ₹600 Cr over coming quarters
$22-23 Mn sales potential at full capacity

highlights: The Gujarat PEB plant began operations on July 9, with Phase 2 scheduled for October
Andhra Pradesh heavy-structure trial production began, with commercial production expected by August-September
About 35% of the order book comes from new-age sectors, multistory buildings, data centers and hotels
Installed capacity rose to 221,000 tonnes after Gujarat Phase 1
The planned Canada-focused export unit targets 15,000 tonnes and EBITDA margin above 20% at scale
Management expects exports and complex heavy structures to improve the margin profile over time
Interarch Building Solutions Ltd.quote: "We are well on target for our projections."

fyPerformance: FY26 Revenue: ₹1,898 Cr (+31% YoY); EBITDA: ₹176 Cr (+29% YoY); PAT: ₹135 Cr (+25% YoY)
Order book stood at ₹1,703 Cr as of April 2026
Export orders worth over ₹40 Cr were received in FY26
Spent ₹127 Cr in capex to expand capacities in Andhra Pradesh, Kiccha and Gujarat

guidance.value: ₹3,500 Cr after all capacities come live

highlights: Andhra Pradesh expansion is focused on heavy steel structures
Gujarat PEB plant is located in a major industrial cluster and targets sectors like EVs and semiconductors
Company secured export certifications for Canada and USA
MoU signed with ER Steel for structural steel and PEB business across Canada and North America
Sector tailwinds remain strong from industrial capex, warehousing, logistics, renewable energy, data centres, semiconductors and large manufacturing projects

fyPerformance: Q1FY27 revenue grew about 25% YoY to ₹366 Cr from ₹295 Cr
EBITDA increased to nearly ₹35 Cr from ₹30.9 Cr, while margin moderated to 9.4%
PAT margin declined to 5% from 5.4% due to the roughly 100 bps EBITDA margin impact
Q1 order bookings rose around 150% to ₹580 Cr from ₹240 Cr a year earlier
The closing order book stood at ₹1,376 Cr, providing six to eight months of execution visibility

guidanceTracking.actual: ₹366 Cr in Q1; ₹1,376 Cr order book

highlights: Q1 included the company’s largest order of ₹165 Cr for a solar cell and module facility
Renewables, transformers and wires and cables lead the order mix; logistics contributes about 24-25%
Prefab capacity utilization was above 75%, while the Mambattu sandwich-panel line reached about 45%
The company began exports with insulated sandwich panels supplied to Africa
EPACK Data Center Solutions is targeting structural steel, containment zones and modular data-center opportunities
Management expects margins to normalize as new orders reflect higher steel prices
EPACK Prefab Technologies Ltd.quote: "The ₹1,380 crore order book gives us confidence that we will very easily achieve the growth target."

fyPerformance: FY26 Revenue: ₹1,525 Cr (+35% YoY); EBITDA: ₹160 Cr (+36% YoY); PAT: ₹93 Cr (+56% YoY)
Prefab business grew around 45% YoY in FY26
Capacity utilisation improved through the year and reached 83% in Q4FY26
Operating cash flow stood at ₹136 Cr, around 85% of EBITDA; net cash stood at ₹201 Cr
highlights: Management believes 30% growth is achievable in the prefab division based on order book, pipeline and capacity additions
Order book and pipeline provide strong FY27 visibility
Higher capacity utilisation through FY26 indicates operating leverage potential
Healthy operating cash conversion and net cash position support the next phase of growth
Structural shift from conventional construction to faster, factory-made and execution-efficient solutions remains a key demand driver

fyPerformance: Q1FY27 revenue grew 22.5% YoY to ₹291 Cr, supported by both Phenix and Proflex
Operating EBITDA stood at ₹33 Cr with margin of 11.4%; reported EBITDA was ₹36 Cr
PAT increased 22% to ₹22 Cr from ₹18 Cr
Phenix revenue grew 22% to ₹214 Cr and Proflex revenue grew 25% to ₹77 Cr
Order book rose 25% YoY to ₹1,053 Cr, including ₹278 Cr of export orders

guidanceTracking.actual: Around 15% sustainable at current freight costs

highlights: Phenix and Proflex inquiry pipelines were about ₹4,000 Cr and ₹200 Cr respectively
Sanand PEB capacity will rise from 72,000 to 92,000 tonnes, supporting H2 growth
The board approved ₹30 Cr for an automated heavy-structural-steel line at Sanand
AISC certification at Cheyyar enables US West Coast exports from FY28
Q1 capex was ₹27 Cr across Sanand expansion, Proflex mobile units and captive solar
Higher West Asia freight costs pressured margins, though lower US Section 232 duties provide some offset
M&B Engineering Ltd.quote: "The pipeline reinforces our confidence in delivering on the 25% plus growth guidance for the year."

fyPerformance: FY26 Revenue: ₹1,260 Cr (+27% YoY); PAT: ₹93 Cr (+20% YoY)
Unexecuted order book stood at ₹1,083 Cr, growing 35% YoY
FY26 order inflow stood at ₹1,539 Cr (+28% YoY)
Phenix division FY26 revenue stood at ₹985 Cr (+29% YoY); Proflex division revenue stood at ₹275 Cr (+23% YoY)
highlights: Management has not given specific margin guidance due to uncertainty in steel prices, freight, FX and geopolitical conditions
FY26 capex was ₹33 Cr, while FY27 capex is expected around ₹100 Cr
Company is adding around 20,000 MT capacity at Sanand, expected to be commissioned in Q2FY27
Export revenue is targeted to rise sharply to ₹275-300 Cr in FY27 from ₹165 Cr in FY26
Margin pressure in Q4 was due to FX loss, input cost inflation and freight costs
